title: Independence number equals edge covering number in bipartite graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a finite bipartite graph with vertex classes $X$ and $Y$, and suppose that $G$ has minimum degree $\delta(G) > 0$, so that every vertex is an endpoint of at least one edge. Then the independence number $\alpha(G)$—the greatest number of pairwise non-adjacent vertices—equals the edge covering number $\beta'(G)$, the least number of edges in an edge covering of $G$ (a set of edges meeting every vertex).
hypotheses_covered: G is bipartite with parts X and Y
replaced:
In a bipartite graph $G$ with $\delta > 0$, the number of
vertices in a maximum independent set is equal to the number of edges in a
minimum edge covering.
